answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can route task scheduling through a collateralized staking trellis. Each agent must lock a financial bond in escrow to secure execution rights and harvest protocol nectar, with protocol misbehavior triggering slashing. Unfunded clones are exiled to a sable, zero-priority mempool. An attacker incurs the scarce verifiable cost of locked capital per identity. However, this steep liquidity requirement prices out honest, capital-constrained agents.
